### Workspace layout

```
Cargo.toml                  workspace: members, [workspace.dependencies], [workspace.lints]
clippy.toml                 allow-unwrap-in-tests = true, allow-expect-in-tests = true
crates/bezel-core/          THE HEXAGON. Deps: thiserror ONLY.
  src/domain/               DeviceModel catalog, Orientation, Frame (RGBA8), Rect, DirtyRegion/diff,
                            theme model (Theme, Element, Binding, Style), sensor catalog (SensorId, Reading, Unit),
                            storage model (RemotePath, FileEntry), Confirm, BezelError
  src/ports/                driven: DeviceBus, ScreenLink, SensorSource, FrameRenderer, ThemeStore;
                            driving: DeviceControl, ThemeRuntime (traits only)
  src/app/                  use cases generic over driven ports (no threads, no timers: `tick(now)` style)
crates/bezel-devices/       DRIVEN. protocol/<family>.rs = pure encoders/decoders (bytes in/out, golden-tested);
                            transport/{serial,usb,hid}.rs = I/O; discovery.rs; fake.rs (FakeScreen recorder)
crates/bezel-render/        DRIVEN. FrameRenderer over tiny-skia + cosmic-text + image
crates/bezel-sensors/       DRIVEN. SensorSource: linux/, windows/, nvidia.rs, fake.rs (cfg per OS INSIDE)
crates/bezel-themes/        DRIVEN. ThemeStore: native format (serde DTOs, versioned), importers (python YAML, TURZX .turtheme NRBF)
crates/bezel-cli/           DRIVING (clap) + composition root in main.rs. JSON DTOs live here.
apps/bezel-studio/          Tauri 2. src-tauri/ = driving adapter (commands) + composition root; src/ = web UI
docs/reverse-engineering/   protocol and format specs (the byte-level contract)
packaging/linux/            udev rules (uaccess) and postinstall
scripts/install-local.sh    release build + install into ~/.local (bin, .desktop, icon)
```

Every code unit is exactly one of: core, port (inside core), adapter, composition root. If it does not fit, the design is wrong — stop and mark the task `blocked`.

### Core purity (review-blocking)

- `crates/bezel-core/Cargo.toml` `[dependencies]` = `thiserror` only. No serde, tiny-skia, serialport, nusb, tauri, clap, image. Serialization DTOs live in `bezel-themes` (files) and in the driving adapters (JSON). `bezel-devices`/`bezel-sensors` may appear only under `[dev-dependencies]` for use-case tests with fakes.
- No I/O in core: never `std::fs`, `std::process`, `std::net`, `std::thread`, `std::time::SystemTime::now`. Time and durations are values passed in.
- No `#[cfg(windows)]` / `#[cfg(target_os = ...)]` in core. Platform branching lives in adapters.
- Ports are `pub trait`s in `bezel_core::ports`; signatures use only core types (never `serialport::SerialPort`, never a `String` that is secretly a device path — use `DeviceAddress`).
- Rendering math that must be identical everywhere (dirty-rect diff, value→fraction, formatting of sensor values) is domain and lives in core; pixel rasterization is the renderer adapter.

### Device protocols (the heart of this project)

- Every opcode, header and layout comes from `docs/reverse-engineering/`. Encoders are pure functions returning `Vec<u8>`; each one has a unit test against the verified hex vectors in the docs (golden bytes). Never "guess" a byte: if the spec says unknown, keep the vendor's exact bytes and name the constant `UNKNOWN_*` with a doc comment.
- Frames enter a `ScreenLink` as RGBA8 in the THEME orientation; the adapter rotates to the panel's native orientation and converts the pixel format (RGB565 LE/BE, BGR, BGRA, compressed-BGRA, PNG/JPEG) exactly as the family requires.
- Partial updates: core computes dirty rectangles between the last presented frame and the new one; each family decides how to ship them (rect bitmaps, rev-C row runs, full PNG for TUR_USB).
- Destructive operations (format storage, firmware update, delete remote file, factory reset, reboot) require `Confirm::Yes` in the core use case; only a human-facing driving adapter may pass `Confirm::Yes`.
- Transports: one owner per device handle; a device worker thread in the driving adapter serializes all writes. Timeouts are explicit; retries bounded and logged with `tracing`.
- Discovery never writes to a port. The rev-C MCU wake (open/close of `CT88INCH`/`CT21INCH`/`USB7INCH`) is the only allowed side effect and only when the SoC gadget is absent.
- Hardware tests are `#[ignore]` and gated by env `BEZEL_HW_TESTS=1`. CI never sees a screen. The dev machine has a Turing 8.8" (MCU 1a86:ca88 on /dev/ttyACM0, SoC 0525:a4a7 on /dev/ttyACM1).

### Sensors

- Never fabricate a value: unavailable sensors return `Reading::Unavailable(reason)` and the UI shows it.
- Linux CPU temperature: hwmon `k10temp` (Tctl/Tdie), `zenpower`, `coretemp` ("Package id 0"), then `cpu_thermal`/acpitz fallback; label the source. GPU: NVML first, then amdgpu sysfs, then i915/xe hwmon.
- Rates (network, disk IO) are computed from monotonic counter deltas divided by the real elapsed time passed in, never by the nominal interval.

### UI (apps/bezel-studio/src)

- Static ES modules, no bundler, no framework, no inline scripts (CSP `script-src 'self'`). Every user-facing string goes through `i18n/` (pt-BR + en). Pointer events for in-canvas drag (Tauri's native file-drop owns HTML5 DnD). Keyboard operable; `prefers-color-scheme` and `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured.
- The preview canvas shows frames rendered by the Rust renderer (WYSIWYG); the DOM only draws selection handles and guides.
- Demo mode: a fake bridge when `window.__TAURI__` is absent, so the UI runs in a browser for Playwright.

### Errors

- Core: `BezelError` (thiserror), domain-shaped variants. Adapters map their errors into it; never bubble `serialport::Error`/`nusb` errors through a port.
- `anyhow` only at the top of binaries (CLI `main`, Tauri command boundary).
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!` outside `#[cfg(test)]`.
- `unsafe` is denied workspace-wide; if FFI ever needs it, only in an adapter with a `// SAFETY:` line.

### Tests

- Unit tests next to the code (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) or in `tests.rs` modules; integration tests in `crates/<crate>/tests/`.
- Use-case tests go through the fakes (`FakeScreen` records every byte/frame; `FakeSensors` scripted values).
- Coverage ≥ 80% lines via `cargo llvm-cov --workspace --locked --fail-under-lines 80`; composition roots excluded by the gate's regex.
- A bugfix STARTS with a failing test.

### Style & lints

- `cargo fmt --all` before every commit; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean.
- `//!` crate docs, `///` on every `pub` item in `bezel-core`. No commented-out code. No `TODO`/`FIXME` without `#NN`.
- Functions ≤ 40 lines preferred; guard clauses; enums instead of boolean parameters.

### Commits

- Conventional Commits, scope = phase slug (`feat(device-protocols): ...`). Type by task nature.
- Atomic: 1 task = 1 commit; `Cargo.lock` rides with the task that changed it. Reference `D-XX` in the body when relevant.
- Code, commits, PRs in English; `.jdi/` docs in pt-BR.
- Hooks are active (`core.hooksPath .githooks`): `commit-msg` enforces the header and forbids mixing code with `.jdi/` state; `pre-commit` requires an active phase (CONTEXT.md + PLAN.md staged/committed). Never `--no-verify`.

### Local install (user requirement)

At the end of every phase: `bash scripts/install-local.sh` (release build, install into `~/.local/bin`, desktop entry and icon; no sudo) and report the installed version so the user can test on the real screen.
</conventions>
